idiom_name: Diesel repository: delete + batch insert in one transaction (associations are load-only)
implementation_notes: Rust ORMs deliberately stop at loading: Diesel's associations are child-to-parent only and there is no has-many, so the parent's repository owns the children explicitly - load them with Post::belonging_to(&order) / grouped_by, and on save replace the set with delete + insert inside Connection::transaction. Because the child rows carry no identity beyond (order_id, position) nothing else can reference or load them, which is what makes the replacement safe. This manual form is the faithful one in Diesel; the moment a child needs its own repository or a foreign key from elsewhere, it is no longer a dependent.
pitfalls: The transaction closure must own delete and insert; an insert issued outside it leaves the order without its lines after a failure.
Diesel has no identity map: loading parent and children separately yields two structures, so the repository should return the pair (Order, Vec<OrderLine>) or a derived aggregate.
Batch-inserting an empty slice is a runtime/query error in some backends - guard the empty dependent set instead of relying on the insert to be a no-op.
